prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map supports a corridor layout with the floor extending forward between a close left wall and right-side columns/open edge; bright lower-floor and wall regions are nearest, while the dark upper corridor is farther away. In frame 1, two people are roughly 6–9 m ahead and close to each other; the nearer person then appears about 4–6 m away in frame 2, 3–4 m in frame 3, and approximately 1–2 m away on the right in frame 4, showing a clear approach and rightward passage. A second person remains farther ahead, about 4–7 m away and left of the nearer person in frames 3–4; by frame 5 the main corridor is empty, with only part of a person near the far-right edge. Compared with RGB, the map makes near/far ordering and the continuous floor plane clearer, but distances are only rough: bright wall boundaries bleed into the floor, distant regions lose detail, and people have nearly uniform depth despite their bodies spanning different distances.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map isolates two people in frame 1 near the upper-left portion of the corridor, roughly 6–9 m from the camera and within about 1 m of each other, and also marks a skateboard below the left person. The nearer tracked person shifts from near the center in frame 2 to center-left in frame 3 and then becomes a large mask on the right in frame 4, consistent with approaching from roughly 4–6 m to about 1–2 m; another smaller person stays farther ahead and to the left, about 4–7 m away. The large frame-4 mask shows the nearer person turned partly sideways, with the torso generally facing leftward across the image rather than squarely toward the camera; the map does not reliably establish gaze. It makes instance count, overlap, and the partly out-of-view person at the far-right edge of frame 5 easier to see than RGB, but it omits the corridor surfaces, inconsistently detects the skateboard and distant people, and clips masks and labels at image boundaries.
descriptions.pose: The pose map gives articulated body geometry for one principal person in frames 2–4: the person is upright and several metres ahead in frames 2–3, then much closer on the right in frame 4 with knees and hips flexed and the body turned side-on. The skeleton grows substantially and moves rightward across those frames, supporting an approach from about 4–6 m to roughly 1–2 m, followed by disappearance from view in frame 5. In frame 4, the extended left-side arm and bent legs reveal limb directions and joint heights that are harder to separate in RGB; the visible hand remains well beyond the camera wearer’s arm reach, while the person’s own hands lie within arm’s reach of their torso and legs. The map does not represent the second person, skateboard, walls, or depth directly, and it is unreliable for the small distant figures in frame 1, exact gaze direction, hidden limbs, and the partly cropped person in frame 5.
